1158: The four traditional Maxwell equations are thus replaced by two, thus demonstrating the
1159: economy of tensor notation. More importantly, however, both sides of equations (1.77) and
1160: (1.78) manifestly transform as tensors; therefore, if they are true in one inertial frame, they
1161: must be true in any Lorentz-transformed frame. This is why tensors are so useful in relativity
1162: — we often want to express relationships without recourse to any reference frame, and it is
1163: necessary that the quantities on each side of an equation transform in the same way under
1164: change of coordinates. As a matter of jargon, we will sometimes refer to quantities which
1165: are written in terms of tensors as covariant (which has nothing to do with “covariant”
1166: as opposed to “contravariant”). Thus, we say that (1.77) and (1.78) together serve as the
1167: covariant form of Maxwell’s equations, while (1.73) or (1.74) are non-covariant.

1168:    Let us now introduce a special class of tensors, known as diﬀerential forms (or just
1169: “forms”). A diﬀerential p-form is a (0, p) tensor which is completely antisymmetric. Thus,
1170: scalars are automatically 0-forms, and dual vectors are automatically one-forms (thus ex-
1171: plaining this terminology from a while back). We also have the 2-form Fµν and the 4-form
1172: ǫµνρσ. The space of all p-forms is denoted Λp, and the space of all p-form ﬁelds over a mani-
1173: fold M is denoted Λp(M). A semi-straightforward exercise in combinatorics reveals that the
1174: number of linearly independent p-forms on an n-dimensional vector space is n!/(p!(n −p)!).
1175: So at a point on a 4-dimensional spacetime there is one linearly independent 0-form, four
1176: 1-forms, six 2-forms, four 3-forms, and one 4-form. There are no p-forms for p > n, since all
1177: of the components will automatically be zero by antisymmetry.
1178:   Why should we care about diﬀerential forms? This is a hard question to answer without
1179: some more work, but the basic idea is that forms can be both diﬀerentiated and integrated,
1180: without the help of any additional geometric structure. We will delay integration theory
1181: until later, but see how to diﬀerentiate forms shortly.

1183: product A ∧B by taking the antisymmetrized tensor product:
